extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners involved in ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_short: ex parte reexamination procedure for patents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for conducting and participating in ex parte and inter partes patent reexamination proceedings (amendments, drawings, fees, service, prior art, scope, and timing). Intended to direct examiners and advise patent owners/requesters on required practices and submission content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment paper submission in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment in an ex parte or an inter partes reexamination proceeding is made by filing a paper directing that proposed specified changes be made to the patent specification, including the claims, or to the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment paper may be submitted as an accompaniment to a request by the patent owner in accordance with § 1.510(e), as part of a patent owner statement under § 1.530(b), or, where permitted, during prosecution pursuant to § 1.550(a) or § 1.937.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to original patent drawing sheets are not permitted; any change must be in the form of a new sheet of drawings for each drawing sheet that is changed. Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' added figures as 'New,' and canceled figures must be surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.' Changes may NOT be made on the original patent drawings. See 37 CFR 1.530(d)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated Sheet sketch procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patent owner wishes to change/amend the drawings, the owner should submit an ink sketch showing proposed changes/amendments for approval by the examiner presented as a separate paper clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submitted sketch will be made part of the record. Once approved, substitute or new drawing sheets must be submitted for each sheet to be changed. If a new drawing sheet contains multiple figures, each figure must be marked individually as 'Amended' or 'New' as applicable; it is not sufficient to mark only the header of the sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of new drawing sheets before NIRC and Quayle SSPs
rubrics_metrics.description: New sheets of drawings must be entered into the record in the reexamination file prior to preparation of a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a proposed drawing correction has been approved but new sheets have not been filed and the proceeding is otherwise ready for NIRC, prepare an ex parte Quayle Office action setting an appropriate shortened statutory time period (SSP) for filing the new sheets. If reexamination was requested by a third party, set SSP of ONE MONTH (or 30 days, whichever is longer). If requested by patent owner, ordered under 35 U.S.C.257, or Director ordered, set SSP of TWO MONTHS. If new sheets are not timely filed, the reexamination certificate will be issued without the proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When the correct inventor(s) were not named in the patent being reexamined, the Director may, on petition of all parties and satisfactory proof and payment of fee, include in the reexamination certificate an amendment naming only the actual inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be submitted as part of the reexamination proceeding and must satisfy the requirements of § 1.324. If the petition under § 1.324 is filed but the reexamination concludes other than by a reexamination certificate, a certificate of correction indicating the change of inventorship will be issued upon request. Alternatively, correction by reissue under 35 U.S.C.251 may be appropriate (see MPEP § 1412.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction merges with reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition to correct inventorship is granted during the reexamination proceeding, a separate certificate of correction indicating the change of inventorship will not be issued because the reexamination certificate will contain the appropriate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In effect the certificate of correction is merged with the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of excess claims fees during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees are applicable to excess claims proposed to be added to a patent by their presentation during a reexamination proceeding in accordance with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) and 35 U.S.C.41(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because 35 U.S.C.41(a)(2) provides that an excess claims fee is due 'on filing or on presentation at any other time' (e.g., during reexamination), the fees must be submitted for excess claims presented in a reexamination proceeding on or after December 8, 2004. If amendment only revises existing claims and provides no new claim, no claim fee is due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions triggering independent and total excess claims fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent claims fee (37 CFR 1.20(c)(3)) is due for each independent claim in excess of three and in excess of the number of independent claims in the patent being reexamined. The total claims fee (37 CFR 1.20(c)(4)) is due for each claim in excess of twenty and in excess of the number of claims in the patent being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both limits must be exceeded for the respective fee to apply. The MPEP provides illustrative examples showing various cancel/add scenarios and when fees apply (e.g., adding three independent claims when two were canceled may trigger the independent fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims excluded from fee calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that has been disclaimed under 35 U.S.C.253 and 37 CFR 1.321(a) as of the date of filing of the request for reexamination is not considered to be a claim in the patent for purposes of excess claims fee calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same applies to a claim canceled via a prior reexamination certificate, reissue patent, or certificate of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee deficiency notices and correction time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess claims fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) are not paid with the presentation of the excess claims, a Notice of Defective Paper will be issued requiring correction of the defect (fee deficiency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In third-party requested reexaminations, set a one-month period (form PTOL-475) to correct the defect. In patent owner requested or Director ordered reexaminations, set a two-month period (form PTO-2311). An extension of time to correct may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). If unpaid within the period, prosecution will be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(e). If unpaid in response to a final Office action, notify owner of fee deficiency in the advisory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for filing a petition in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.550(i) and 1.20(c)(6), a petition in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must be accompanied by the petition fee except for listed exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee amounts (per 37 CFR 1.20(c)(6)) are: $2,040 for a large entity; $816 for a small entity; $408 for a micro entity (available for patent owners only). Certain petitions are excepted (e.g., petitions to extend response period under 1.530(c); to accept delayed response under 1.550(e); to accept unintentionally delayed benefit claim under 1.78; petitions under 1.530(l) for correction of inventorship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party requester reply timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to the patent owner’s statement under § 1.530 may be filed by the ex parte reexamination requester within two months from the date of service of the patent owner’s statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must be served upon the patent owner in accordance with § 1.248. There are no extensions of time. The reply need not be limited to issues raised in the statement and may include additional prior art and any issue appropriate for reexamination. If the patent owner does not file a statement, no reply or other submission from the requester will be considered. The requester may not file further papers after the reply; any further papers will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and proof-of-service for consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file or serve the documents set forth in § 1.530 or § 1.535 may result in their being refused consideration; no submissions other than the statement (1.530) and the reply (1.535) will be considered prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely submissions will ordinarily not be considered. Untimely papers (other than untimely patent owner papers after the response period) will not be placed of record but returned. Any paper requiring proof of service filed without proof may be denied consideration; the Central Reexamination Unit should inquire with sender whether service was made. See MPEP §§ 2266.03 and 2267.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner consideration of submitted matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Once reexamination is ordered, any submissions properly filed and served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530 and 1.535 will be considered by the examiner when preparing the first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of proposed amendments to the specification including claims will be guided by 1.530(d)-(j). Consideration of the patent owner’s statement guided by 1.530(c). Consideration of requester’s reply guided by 1.535. Issues not previously presented but within scope will be treated in the Office action; issues outside the scope should be treated pursuant to 1.552(c). For handling of new matter see MPEP § 2270.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of ex parte reexamination proceedings (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the times for filing the statement and reply have expired, reexamination will be conducted according to procedures established for initial examination under sections 132 and 133, and will be conducted with special dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner may propose any amendment and new claims to distinguish the invention from prior art cited under section 301 or in response to an adverse decision; no proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim will be permitted. Proceedings (including appeals) are to be concluded with special dispatch within the Office (35 U.S.C.305).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response period and extensions in ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.550)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be given at least thirty days to respond to any Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses may include further statements and/or proposed amendments or new claims. Requests for extension must specify the period and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g). Extension request timing and permissibility differs by type of reexamination (third-party requested vs patent-owner requested or Director ordered); generally extensions in patent owner requested or Director ordered reexamination will not be more than two months absent sufficient cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination for failure to respond and revival
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action or any written statement of an interview required under § 1.560(b), the prosecution in the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution, and the Director will proceed to issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination proceeding under § 1.570 in accordance with the last action of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a response is not timely filed, a petition under § 1.137 may be filed to revive a reexamination prosecution terminated under this paragraph if the delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements and third-party participation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248; the document must reflect service or it may be refused consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The active participation of the ex parte requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535; no further submissions by the requester will be considered. No submissions on behalf of any third parties will be acknowledged or considered unless in accordance with § 1.510 or § 1.535 or entered in the patent file prior to the date of the order for ex parte reexamination pursuant to § 1.525.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of prior art to be considered by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the discussion, the examiner must consider patents and printed publications cited by another reexamination requester under 1.510 or 1.915; cited in patent owner’s statement under 1.530 or requester’s reply under 1.535 if they comply with 1.98; cited by the patent owner under duty of disclosure (1.555) in compliance with 1.98; discovered by the examiner in searching; of record in the patent file from earlier examination; and of record in the patent file from any 1.501 submission prior to date of an order if it complies with 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where documents are submitted by a party in compliance with the rules, the degree of consideration will normally be limited by the degree to which the filing party has explained the content and relevance. See list (A)-(F) in MPEP § 2256. Provide legible copies as required by 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2) (foreign patents, publications or portion that caused listing, pending unpublished U.S. application portions, and other information or portions which caused listing). Do not submit copies of copending proceedings/applications; instead provide application/proceeding number and status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions filed after NIRC—requirements to interrupt publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the NIRC has been mailed and the proceeding forwarded for publication of the reexamination certificate, a submission of patents/printed publications or other information after NIRC requires special justification to interrupt the printing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission must be accompanied by (A) a factual accounting explaining why the information could not have been submitted earlier, (B) an unequivocal statement that one or more claims are unpatentable, and (C) an amendment to such claim(s) and explanation how the amendment causes the claim(s) to be patentable. This must be provided via a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 (with the petition fee). These requirements are necessary to provide a basis for interrupting the proceeding after NIRC consistent with the Office's statutory mandate for 'special dispatch.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of prior art on forms and entitlement to entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination request must provide a listing of the patents and printed publications as provided in 37 CFR 1.98. The examiner must list on a form PTO-892 (if not already listed) all prior art patents or printed publications cited in the decision on the request, applied in making rejections, or cited as pertinent during reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All citations listed on PTO-892 and all citations not lined-through on PTO/SB/08 or PTO/SB/42 will be the list of prior art considered in the reexamination. A submission is entitled to entry and citation in the reexamination certificate when it complies with 1.98 and is submitted: (A) by the patent owner in the statement under 1.530; (B) by the requester in the reply under 1.535; (C) prior to the order of reexamination under 1.501 by any party; and/or (D) by the patent owner under duty of disclosure 1.555.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.552)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted in the reexamination proceeding, on the basis of the requirements of 35 U.S.C.112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims will not be permitted to enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent. Issues other than those indicated in paragraphs (a) and (b) (i.e., patentability based on patents/printed publications and 35 U.S.C.112 for added/deleted matter) will not be resolved in reexamination; if raised, they will be noted by the examiner and the patent owner may consider filing a reissue application to have such issues considered. Any statement of the patent owner of record may be used after a reexamination proceeding has been ordered to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim when applying patents or printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C.257 special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C.257 will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.530 through 1.570 except that certain differences apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 257: (1) The patent owner will not have right to file a statement under 1.530; (2) Reexamination may be conducted on the basis of any item of information as set forth in 1.605 and is not limited to patents and printed publications; (3) Issues in addition to patents/printed publications and added/deleted subject matter may be considered and resolved; (4) Information material to patentability will be defined by 1.56(b).
